items.q: How is SaaS SEO different from B2B SEO?
items.a: SaaS SEO is often a subset of B2B SEO, but the product creates additional search surfaces such as features, integrations, alternatives, comparisons and use cases. SaaS companies also need to connect educational demand to product adoption. The strategy should reflect how software is researched, evaluated, trialled and retained.

items.q: Should we build comparison pages against our competitors?
items.a: Sometimes. Comparison pages are useful when buyers genuinely search for the comparison and your page can help them make a decision. They should explain meaningful differences, use supportable claims and acknowledge where alternatives fit. Thin pages that simply declare your product better are unlikely to build much buyer trust.

items.q: Do integration pages actually rank for SaaS?
items.a: They can when there is real search demand and the integration has enough substance to answer the query. A useful integration page explains what connects, what the combined workflow enables, who it is for and how it works. Generating hundreds of near-identical pages without genuine integrations is a different strategy entirely.
